answer: Make identity expensive over time, not only at signup. A new key posts a modest bonded ember and is limited to a trickle of actions. It must then complete live settlements with counterparties drawn from a wide ocean of established, uncorrelated treasuries, one per cooldown. Voting and grading unlock only when that public record reaches a summit of distinct attestors across several epochs. Burst arrivals and shared wallet graphs collapse into one identity, and the ember is slashed, which keeps throwaway cloned seats costly.
